title: Media queries use only the declared breakpoints

values: component source files (e.g. tsx/jsx/vue/svelte) that may carry style blocks or CSS-in-JS
facts.note: Only the file extension is observable from the path; it says a file CAN contain styles, not that it contains an @media query.

values: file content contains an @media query with a width condition
facts.note: Content-dependent: requires a scanner that parses @media width conditions (min-width/max-width and range syntax) in stylesheets, style blocks and CSS-in-JS; extension alone cannot establish it.
Vendored and generated trees are never scanned.
Edits to the configuration (frontend.breakpoints) can invalidate existing media queries anywhere in scope.

values: frontend.breakpoints entry added, removed or changed
facts.note: Diff-level observer for media-query width changes and for breakpoint configuration edits; a configuration edit requires re-checking every existing query in scope.

values: bun_responsive_detector: undeclared breakpoint (any width condition in scope, including pre-existing ones)
facts.note: Detector finding comparing every in-scope media-query width to frontend.breakpoints in atdd-bun.yaml, applying the max-width tolerance and em/rem conversion.

fires: A stylesheet adds `@media (min-width: 900px)` when 900 is not in `frontend.breakpoints`.
A component style uses range syntax `width >= 700px` with an undeclared width.
A `max-width: 900px` query exists while the breakpoints are the defaults (480, 768, 1024, 1280): 900 is neither declared nor within 1px below a declared breakpoint.
An existing, unchanged query `@media (min-width: 1280px)` is left in place after 1280 is removed from `frontend.breakpoints`.
A pre-existing query in scope uses an undeclared width (the obligation covers every width condition, not only newly written ones).
doesNotFire: A query uses `min-width: 768px` or `max-width: 767.98px` / `767px` with 768 declared.
A query uses `min-width: 48em` (= 768px at 16px) with 768 declared.
A media query with no width condition (e.g. `prefers-color-scheme`, `print`).

given: A stylesheet or component style outside vendored/generated trees contains an `@media` width condition (`min-width`/`max-width` or range syntax such as `width >= 768px`, `768px <= width`). Term frontend_settings: `atdd-bun.yaml` → `frontend.breakpoints` (the widths media queries may use) and `frontend.viewports` (the widths responsive specs render at; the smallest bounds fixed widths).
when: Any media-query width condition in scope exists or is added/changed, or `frontend.breakpoints` is edited so existing conditions must be re-checked.
then: Every width in every such condition MUST be one of the breakpoints declared under `frontend.breakpoints` in `atdd-bun.yaml` (default 480, 768, 1024, 1280); a `max-width` within 1px below a breakpoint (`767px`, `767.98px`) counts as that breakpoint, and `em`/`rem` convert to px at 16px.
prefer: During GREEN: reuse an existing declared breakpoint that expresses the required layout transition.
During GREEN: add one breakpoint to `frontend.breakpoints` only when the current design genuinely requires a distinct transition width.
During GREEN: change only the affected media query or configuration entry.
avoid: Using an undeclared one-off width as a shortcut.
Adding speculative breakpoints for future devices.
Normalizing unrelated responsive rules while fixing this one.
unless: The file lives in a vendored or generated tree (`node_modules`, `dist`, `build`, `_generated`); these are never scanned.
why: CSS custom properties cannot be used in media queries, so breakpoints cannot be tokens; declaring them once and requiring every query to use them keeps layouts switching at the same widths everywhere instead of at a new one per component.
evidence: Every affected media-query width is declared in `frontend.breakpoints` (bun_responsive_detector reports no finding).
The current responsive acceptance passes at the relevant viewports (`frontend.viewports`, the widths responsive specs render at).
verifier_detail: Check every width condition in `@media`: `min-width`/`max-width` and range syntax (`width >= 768px`, `768px <= width`).
A `max-width` X matches breakpoint B when X == B or B-1 <= X < B (within 1px below, e.g. `767px`, `767.98px` for 768).
`em`/`rem` convert to px at 16px before matching.
Term frontend_settings: `atdd-bun.yaml` → `frontend.viewports` (the widths responsive specs render at; the smallest bounds fixed widths) and `frontend.breakpoints` (the widths media queries may use).
Severity 3; disposition strict (source: 'New in atdd-bun, strict.').
audit: summary: Media queries use only the declared breakpoints.

additions.text: Media queries without width conditions (prefers-color-scheme, print) do not fire.
additions.justification: Clarifies scope implied by 'every width condition'; adds no obligation.

additions.text: Configuration edits to frontend.breakpoints that invalidate existing queries fire the rule.
additions.justification: Consequence of the source's universal 'every width condition MUST use a declared breakpoint' and its fix hint mentioning configuration entries; adds no new obligation.
The tolerance/em-rem rules and frontend_settings term semantics were required by the auditor to sit beside the coder obligation; losslessness wins over brevity.

trace.note: Heading for the canonical path, which is the then obligation.
'During GREEN' qualifier retained as prefix of each prefer item.
